name: libcello
why: A library bringing higher-level features like generics and classes to C, a fascinating look at pushing C into new shapes.

brief.what_it_is: Cello is a C library that adds higher-level programming features to ordinary C: generic data structures, polymorphic functions, interfaces or type classes, constructors and destructors, optional garbage collection, exceptions, and reflection. A program includes Cello.h, creates objects on the stack with $(Type, value) or on the heap with new(Type, ...), and loops over collections with foreach. The output is a normal C program that links against libCello.a. The example programs print typed values and walk arrays and tables.
brief.why_it_exists: Daniel Holden made it as a fun experiment to see what C looks like hacked to its limits, and says it should interest anyone who wants to explore what is possible in C.
brief.how_it_works: The README itself does not explain the mechanism. It points readers to the article 'A Fat Pointer Library' for an overview of how Cello works, and says the source code is fairly readable. Cello is described as a runtime system layered on standard C.

brief.install_notes: Cello is a plain C library, so you download the source tarball from the download link on libcello.org, unpack it, and build it. It needs a gnu99-compatible C compiler: gcc on Linux, Xcode with command line tools on Mac (clang), and MinGW64 or Cygwin on Windows. Build with make, check with make check, then optionally make install. No accounts, runtimes or hardware are mentioned. The installation page says installing a C library is not always trivial and suggests searching general C help if you get stuck.
brief.standout: It is a runtime library that makes C feel like a higher-level language without a new compiler or syntax: the code is ordinary C that includes one header. The author openly calls it a hack and presents it as an exploration of how far C can be pushed.
brief.status: unknown. The README and installation page mention a 'latest release' and a download link but show no release date, version number or last-commit date. The author's FAQ says Cello 'does aim to be production ready'. The homepage and GitHub README were both reachable.
brief.caveats: Written in C with a gnu99-compatible compiler required. Windows needs MinGW64 or Cygwin. The author says it is a hack with 'its fair share of oddities and pitfalls' and recommends it for hobby projects before teams or deadlines. He says no high-profile project he knows of uses it, and that it is 'too big and scary a dependency for new C projects if they want to be portable and easy to maintain'. Make install may fail, in which case manual installation is needed. The license is in LICENSE.md, but the README does not name it.
quotes: I made Cello as a fun experiment to see what C looks like hacked to its limits.
Although Cello does not look like it - it is just a C library.
Cello does aim to be production ready, but because it is a hack it has its fair share of oddities and pitfalls
